Package dev.opencollab.paletter

Class Paletter.Builder

java.lang.Object
dev.opencollab.paletter.Paletter.Builder
Enclosing class:
Paletter
public static final class Paletter.Builder extends Object
Configures the global policy of a Paletter: everything that is the same for every palette it compiles.

Not thread safe: configure on one thread, then share the built Paletter. Every method throws NullPointerException for a null argument and returns this builder.

Since:
1.0.0

    • experiments

      public @NonNull Paletter.Builder experiments(@NonNull String... toggles)
      Enables experiment toggles (e.g. y_2026_drop_4) in every version. By default none is enabled: the items and blocks a version has only behind a toggle are missing in its palette, so the Fallbacks apply to them like to content the version lacks altogether (and force is only for content that is really there). The items stay in the item registry (Palette.itemDefinitions()) all the same: BDS registers them in a world without the toggle too, it only leaves them out of everything else (the creative inventory, for one). An enabled toggle makes its content present in the versions that gate it; those palettes list the toggle in Palette.experiments() and send it with Palette.applyTo(org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.packet.StartGamePacket). A palette tells the toggle of a piece of content with Palette#experimentOf, and its report has a line for every toggle left disabled. Every call adds to the toggles of the earlier ones.
      Parameters:
      toggles - the toggle ids, as BDS names them
      Returns:
      this builder
      Since:
      1.0.0

    • experiments

      public @NonNull Paletter.Builder experiments(@NonNull DataVersion version, @NonNull String... toggles)
      Enables experiment toggles in one version only, in addition to those of experiments(String...). The version must be one this instance serves, or build() throws an IllegalArgumentException. Every call adds to the toggles of the earlier ones. Toggles that gate nothing in a version are ignored there; for a toggle enabled for one version the palette's report says so.
      Parameters:
      version - the data version
      toggles - the toggle ids, as BDS names them
      Returns:
      this builder
      Since:
      1.0.0

    • allExperiments

      public @NonNull Paletter.Builder allExperiments()
      Enables every experiment toggle each version gates content with, except the voxel shape experiment, which changes how the client treats shapes instead of adding content. The content behind the toggles is present, as in the raw data of the version; the palettes list the toggles in Palette.experiments(). Lookups with a Lookup see that content then. Adds to experiments(String...) (the union is enabled). The voxel shape experiment is enabled only by naming it: experiments("voxel_shapes").
      Returns:
      this builder
      Since:
      1.0.0

    • reports

      public @NonNull Paletter.Builder reports(@NonNull Consumer<PaletteReport> reports)
      Sets where the compilation reports go.
      Parameters:
      reports - called once for each palette compiled (with this instance's layers applied), with its report, and once with a one entry report for the first palette served for a protocol newer than the newest data (PaletteReport.NEWER_PROTOCOL; that note has no unknownBlocks or unknownItems). Called outside any internal lock: it may use this Paletter. The default logs each entry to the System.Logger dev.opencollab.paletter: warnings at WARNING, the rest at DEBUG
      Returns:
      this builder
      Since:
      1.0.0

    • failOn

      public @NonNull Paletter.Builder failOn(@NonNull Predicate<PaletteReport.Entry> failOn)
      Makes report entries fatal: build() throws a PaletteException for a palette whose report has an entry the predicate accepts, after the reports consumer got the report. For example failOn(entry -> entry.level() == PaletteReport.Level.WARNING) fails on every warning. It applies to the palettes this instance compiles; the report of Palette.extend(dev.opencollab.paletter.PaletteLayer) is the caller's to check.
      Parameters:
      failOn - which entries are fatal; default none
      Returns:
      this builder
      Since:
      1.0.0

      Loads the behaviour values (Palette.resolve(dev.opencollab.paletter.vanilla.BedrockBlockState).behaviour(), ResolvedItem#behaviour()) with the palettes, or not. Off, the behaviour data is never read or kept, and asking for a behaviour value throws IllegalStateException; resolutions and everything else work as before.     • build

      public @NonNull Paletter build()
      Creates the Paletter and compiles the palette of every served version now, so no later call waits for data: each palette is built with everything its lookups use (behaviour values unless off, voxel shapes, creative content, lookup tables). The versions compile at the same time, on a few threads of their own (at most one per processor) that end with this call; the palettes are the same as compiled one after another. Each is passed to the reports consumer on the calling thread, oldest version first. Narrow the versions with versions(Predicate) to compile fewer.
      Returns:
      the Paletter
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if versions(Predicate) accepts no data version, or experiments are enabled for a version it does not accept
      PaletteException - if a report has an entry failOn(Predicate) accepts
      PaletteException - if a layer cannot be compiled: the first version's failure, after the palettes that compiled were reported
      UncheckedIOException - if the data source cannot be read
      Since:
      1.0.0
